title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical claims can be checked here; it is a table of contents. The page numbering of 15° is missing (blank), and 13° was revised (strike-outs), which shows the statement of a 'conjecture de compatibilité' was being reformulated.

ideas.what: Schematic envelope of a discrete group (universal pro-algebraic group receiving Γ), treated in the metabelian case via extensions with abelian kernel; unipotent / quasi-unipotent sections
ideas.modern_name: pro-algebraic / relative Malcev completion (relative unipotent completion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev (unipotent completion); Deligne (relative completion idea, 1989); Hain (relative completion, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted at in La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this detailed metabelian treatment is not known to me in print.

ideas.what: Fermat tower as the metabelian quotient of π₁ of P¹−{0,1,∞}, realised inside SL(2,ℤ)/[Γ₀,Γ₀] with Γ₀ = [SL2ℤ, SL2ℤ] (punctured j=0 curve), with an 𝔖₃ × Ẑ* action
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the metabelian quotient of the profinite free group / Fermat tower (Ihara's universal power series for Jacobi sums)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. Ihara (Annals 1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); G. Anderson, R. Coleman (late 1980s)

ideas.what: Relation of the Fermat tower module with generalized Jacobians of Fermat curves
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on Tate modules of (generalized) Fermat Jacobians; Jacobi-sum Hecke characters
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (Jacobi sums); Ihara, Anderson ('hyperadelic gamma function'), Coleman

ideas.what: Image of Γ_ℚ in Ẑ⋊Ẑ* and Kummer extensions as a quotient of the Galois action on the metabelian tower
ideas.modern_name: Kummer/cyclotomic characters, Soulé-type characters at low level
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Kummer theory); Deligne, Ihara for the π₁ context

missed.claim: Grothendieck worked out, in undated continuation notes probably from around 1981, an extended study (~80 pages) of the Fermat tower as the metabelian layer of the Galois–Teichmüller tower. It includes the Ẑ*×𝔖₃ symmetry, splittings of the extension by M̂, a 'compatibility' characterisation of the Fermat tower, and links to generalized Jacobians. This topic is credited to Ihara (1984–86), Anderson and Coleman; Grothendieck's priority or independent approach is not recorded.
missed.quote: 51. Exemple : la tour de Fermat … 12°) Scindages de l'extension G_{ρ,σ}/μ de Ẑ*×𝔖₃ par M̂ … 14°) Relation avec jacobiennes généralisées
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: His approach through SL(2,ℤ)/[Γ₀,Γ₀] and schematic envelopes differs from Ihara's power-series method. It may give an alternative, more group-scheme-theoretic description of the metabelian Galois image and the Jacobi-sum characters.

missed.claim: A theory of schematic envelopes of discrete groups in the metabelian case, with a universal characterisation and 'quasi-unipotent sections', predating published relative completion theory.
missed.quote: 50. Enveloppes schématiques de groupes discrets : cas métabélien … 5°) Caract.n universelle de l'env. schématique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relative completions of mapping class and modular groups (Hain) are central today. An independent early Grothendieck version, with a special treatment of quasi-unipotent sections, could be of historical and possibly technical interest.

missed.claim: 'Réflexions sur le th. de Fermat' via the Galois action on the Fermat tower; the content is unknown from this page alone.
missed.quote: 16°) Réflexions sur le th. de Fermat
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest: it would document Grothendieck's view of FLT through anabelian / Galois–Teichmüller methods.

deep.surprise_reason: Only a table of contents, but it documents a substantial, apparently unpublished Grothendieck treatment of the Fermat tower and metabelian schematic envelopes. This anticipates or parallels Ihara's and Hain's later work, which is not credited to him. The actual content cannot be assessed from this page.
transcription_corrections: 'nitabélien[?]' should almost certainly read 'métabélien' (twice, in the title of §50 and in 4°).
In 6°, the struck/unclear beginning reads 'Les suites'.
In 6°, the quotient written 𝔻^∧₁₂ is probably a variant of 𝔻*₁₂ / D̂₁₂.
The page number for 15° is missing; 725' and 733 at the bottom refer to 16° and the end of the section.
